name: vwap_slope_trend_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, large institutional TWAP and VWAP execution algorithms are benchmarked against session VWAP — when they need to buy, they systematically lift offers at progressively higher prices, causing the VWAP slope to rise. At 5-second resolution, the 3-minute VWAP slope (linreg over 36 bars) captures this institutional directional pressure before it fully manifests in price. When the 1-minute slope (12 bars) exceeds the 3-minute slope, it signals that institutional demand is accelerating, not plateauing — the executing TWAP order has not finished and the remaining flow will push NIFTY spot another 10-20 points in the same direction. This acceleration window is the entry trigger: buy CE when slope is positive and building, buy PE when slope is negative and deepening, holding for the next 60-90 seconds while institutional execution continues.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset each session
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP — the institutional benchmark. No scaling needed; it's a full-session cumulative measure.

indicators.name: vwap_slope_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute VWAP slope — primary directional signal. Original used 20 bars at 1-min (20 min). We do NOT use 12x (240 bars = 20 min) because we're trading 30-90s holds. A 3-minute slope detects the institutional order being executed NOW, not a trend from an hour ago. Shorter = more responsive to active flow; longer = too lagged for 30s entries.

indicators.name: vwap_slope_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute VWAP slope — acceleration detector. When slope_12 > slope_36, institutional buying is ramping up (algorithm is behind schedule and increasing urgency). This is the key condition distinguishing a trend beginning from one topping out. Not in the original, added because 5s bars let us detect acceleration within the 3-min trend.

indicators.name: slope_ma_18
indicators.purpose: 90-second SMA of the 3-min slope — ensures the slope itself is building, not reverting. Original had vwap_slope_ma over 10 bars (10 min). Scaled to 18 bars (90s) to match our faster trade timescale. Filters entries where slope is present but decaying.

indicators.name: ema_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute EMA — confirms price in short-term uptrend. Original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars (9 min). We use 36 bars (3 min) rather than 108 bars (9x12) because for a 30-90s trade, price must be above the 3-min EMA to confirm trend; the 9-min EMA would be too slow to add information beyond VWAP itself.

buy_ce.confirmation: All five conditions simultaneously on same bar

buy_pe.confirmation: All five conditions simultaneously on same bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points. When VWAP slope is positive and accelerating, the index should not retrace 8 spot points within the first 30 seconds; if it does, the institutional flow thesis is invalidated. NIFTY 30s typical move is 2-5 option points — a 4-point adverse move indicates the signal was wrong, not normal noise.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. Institutional TWAP continuations on NIFTY driven by active slope-positive flow typically extend 15-25 spot points within 60-90 seconds. 7 option points captures ~50-60% of the expected move at delta 0.5, with 1:1.75 R:R. NIFTY 1-min typical move is 3-7 option points — 7 is the upper end, appropriate for a trend-confirmed signal.

filters.vix_filter: none — VWAP slope trend works across volatility regimes as it captures active order flow
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:25 (VWAP slope needs 5 min of data to stabilize) or after 15:20
filters.volume_filter: implicit — VWAP is volume-weighted, so slope is naturally stronger when volume is higher
filters.trend_filter: vwap_slope_36 > slope_ma_18 ensures slope is building, filtering decaying trends
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — VWAP slope analysis is proprietary but computable; edge persists while institutional TWAP algorithms remain dominant on NIFTY

adaptation_notes: Original was a 20-60 minute equity strategy on NIFTY200 stocks using 1-min bars. Key changes: (1) Universe from equity stocks to NIFTY index — the thesis actually strengthens because NIFTY is dominated by institutional TWAP/VWAP flow, not retail; (2) Lookback compressed from 20 bars (20 min) to 36 bars (3 min) because we trade 30-90s holds, not 20-60 min — we want the slope of the currently-executing order, not a historical trend; (3) Added slope_12 acceleration condition — at 5s resolution we can distinguish an accelerating slope from a flattening one, which 1-min bars cannot; (4) Dropped ADX — irrelevant at 5s frequency, replaced by slope-vs-slope-MA filter which directly tests whether the trend signal is building; (5) Stops/targets calibrated to 5s NIFTY option point magnitudes rather than percentage-based.
weaknesses: VWAP slope is lagging — by bar 36, the institutional order may be 80% complete and the remaining 20% may reverse
Acceleration condition (slope_12 > slope_36) fires late in a move when the trend is about to exhaust, not at the start
At 5-second resolution, single large-volume bars can distort VWAP and create false slope readings
NIFTY closing 30 min (3:00-3:30) sees programmatic buying that creates slope signals not backed by directional institutional flow
